whatThisLaneWasAskedToDo: Establish the CAUSE of the stroke-only flattened widget appearances that VF90 recorded as matching no /AP /N stream in each family's pinned sources, and repair what the cause turns out to be. Invented ink is removed; the form's own ink is restored.

theCauseOnThisHost.answer: RESTORE, NOT REMOVE. On this build host every unaccounted stream is a source /AP /N /Off appearance minus its opaque background fill, and the fill is load-bearing.
theCauseOnThisHost.howItWasEstablished: The unaccounted streams across the five claimed families reduce to FOUR distinct byte sequences. Each was compared, token by token, against the /AP /N streams the pinned sources ship, with one leading opaque rectangle fill normalised away from both sides. Four of four resolve, nothing left over.

derivation.shippedBy: the OCA petition and the Statement of Inability

theCauseOnThisHost.whyTheAccountingToolCalledThemUNMATCHED: Not because the fill colour was unrecognised -- its LEADING_FILL regex does match `1 g`. Two other gaps. FIRST, the regex is anchored at ^ and strips the fill together with the whitespace in front of it, so the SOURCE skeleton begins at `0.501953 g` while the DELIVERED stream, which had the fill removed in place, still begins with the two newlines left behind where it stood. The two skeletons then differ by two whitespace bytes and the SHA-256 comparison separates them. SECOND, the order's /Off opens `q` before its fill, so the fill is not at ^ at all and the regex never fires on that stream. Both are gaps in the normaliser, not evidence about provenance. account-stroke-only-against-pinned-sources.mjs was NOT run -- it rewrites the shared ledger for all 53 families and this lane holds five.
theCauseOnThisHost.whatTheStrippedFillWasDoing: It is not decoration and it is not invisible. Rendering the pinned Statement of Inability THREE ways at 600 dpi settles it: with every annotation removed, the court's own page prints a small square check box; as the source ships, the widget's /AP /N /Off paints an opaque white rectangle over that printed box and then strokes its own LARGER bevelled box, so the participant sees ONE box; in the delivered packet, with the fill stripped, the court's printed box shows through INSIDE the stamped appearance box. Two frames at every check box. This is the same defect FIX01 measured on co_petition_seal_arrest-set, on a different form.
theCauseOnThisHost.soTheRemedy: Restore the authored blank-state paint. Removing this ink would have erased a box the court itself prints -- the over-suppression the cohort has already paid for once.

howTheRepairWasMade.mechanism: scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-active-content.mjs already carries the remedy: stripWidgetBackground({ preserveAuthoredPaint }), reached through the finalizeOfficialForm option preserveUnwrittenSelectionBackgrounds. The ledger's own builderOptsIn: false was the exact field. The repair is that opt-in in the family's builder and nothing else.
howTheRepairWasMade.blastRadius: The flag is opt-in and gated on unwritten AND (PDFCheckBox or PDFRadioGroup) AND disposition PRESERVE_SOURCE_APPEARANCE. /MK /BG is still cleared, so no background is ever requested that the source did not author. Written fields, other field types and every family that does not pass it are byte-unaffected.
howTheRepairWasMade.notDoneHere: No shared script was changed, no ledger shared with other families was rewritten, and no other family's builder was touched.
